answer: Each agent posts a 70-credit bond for one island census district in the knoll register, listing households under a key-bound seal. The knoll auditor recounts each district: if the delta between claim and recount exceeds two, or one household appears under two keys, the bond burns. The first costs 30; the kth costs 30+4(k-1), since later districts lie farther out, so the 1,000th costs 4,026 and 1,000 false districts cost 2,028,000 plus 70,000 in bonds. A rented-census ring fails because one key cannot sign two seals in one epoch. An honest agent pays 30 once and recovers it after a recount.
